title: HÄMA-LIND: Communication regarding palliative care for hemato-oncological patients
summary:
Hematological cancers are cancers of the blood-forming system. They include leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma. These diseases differ widely in their course: some can now be treated very effectively, while others are still not curable despite modern therapies. Many patients experience a high symptom burden, including fatigue, pain, nausea, shortness of breath, and limitations in daily life.

Palliative care can improve the quality of life of patients with serious and life-limiting illnesses. It helps to identify and treat symptoms early and supports both patients and their relatives. In hematology-oncology, however, it is often difficult to talk about palliative care at an early stage. Patients and healthcare professionals may be unsure what the term means and may associate it with dying or a loss of hope.

The aim of this study is therefore to understand how hematological cancer patients perceive the term “palliative care,” what associations they have with it, and how they would prefer to be informed about this topic. Patients will be interviewed about this. The findings are intended to improve communication about palliative care and support early, needs-based care for these patients.
conditions: Patients who are suffering from palliative cancer

interventions.name: Semi-structured interviews with hemato-oncological patients. Focus group interview (360°). Cognitive interviews (hematological patients). Qualitative content analysis of the interviews. Sociodemographic questionnaire with descriptive analysis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosis of a hemato-oncological disease
• Capacity to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients whose general condition is too poor or who are too burdened to participate in a study of any kind
• Cognitive or communicative deficits
• Life expectancy of a few days
